Why building a deals catalogue is hard

Content goes stale fast

A hand-built deals list is out of date the day after you publish it, and keeping it fresh is a full-time job.

You hold the risk

Buying inventory to resell means carrying stock, chasing merchants, and eating what does not sell.

Fraud lands on you

Static codes get copied and reused, and the chargebacks and support tickets are yours.

The play

How listing works

  1. 1

    Pull the catalogue

    Read live, machine-readable Pass inventory from the exchange — each Pass eligible for every channel it fits.

  2. 2

    Surface offers

    Show them in your marketplace, super-app or AI assistant. The same object whether it came from the marketplace, a draw, or a tap point.

  3. 3

    Transact

    A user claims or buys. The Pass is issued tokenised and single-use, and lands in their Vault.

  4. 4

    Settle

    Pricing, validation and settlement are handled by the exchange. You earn on what sells, reconciled per Pass.

What the listing API gives you

Machine-readable inventory

A standard interface AI agents and apps can read, match and transact against — the same inventory the marketplace runs on.

One listing, every channel

Each Pass is eligible for every channel it fits, so you surface the right offers without manual curation.

No inventory risk

You list and surface; the exchange prices, validates and settles. You carry no stock.

Fraud-proof by design

Every Pass is tokenised and consumed once, even after changing hands, so there is nothing to charge back.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I have to buy inventory to list it?

No. Listing surfaces live exchange inventory. Pricing, validation and settlement are handled for you; you earn on what sells.

Is the inventory machine-readable for an AI agent?

Yes. It is a standard interface AI shopping agents can read, match and transact against — the same inventory behind the marketplace.

How is fraud handled?

Every Pass is tokenised and consumed once, even after it changes hands, so copied or reused codes simply fail.

REST or MCP?

Both, with a sandbox on signup. Use whichever your platform speaks.
